A CR taken out of the batch goes to the backlog or `3-ready`, never the inbox, with `formerly.json`; a release or fix CR leaves only to the trash. `triage <item> --inbox` sends an item back to the inbox; `restore` brings a trashed one back to the inbox, on the user's word only.

The folder moves, it is never copied: `1-inbox/`, `2-backlog/P1…P4/`, `3-ready/`, then in the running batch `4-batch/1-pending/` (a CR arrives by `open` or `order add`, the latter from the destination the user chose at "grilled enough?"), `2-actives/` (taken by a Driver), `3-done/` (merged, until `close`), then `5-archives/<YYMMDD-HHMM>-<number>-<slug>/` (after `close`, the merge's time) or, after `order drop`, `6-trash/`, always with its work. A CR taken out of the batch keeps its number and goes to the backlog or `3-ready`, never the inbox (`order drop` refuses it), with `formerly.json`; when that folder joins a batch it gets its number back, and its branch and PR while the branch exists, and `formerly.json` is deleted; a release or fix CR leaves only to the trash. `triage <item> --inbox` sends a backlog or `3-ready` item back to the inbox; `restore <6-trash/item> [--slug <name>]` brings a trashed one back to the inbox, on the user's word only, without its date or batch number, with a line `formerly CR-<n> of batch-<m>`.

It runs no git command that changes anything and no forge command beyond `forge-stack` and the reads of `ship`, `take`, `round` and `handoff`. The agents create worktrees, commit, rebase, push and open and merge PRs with `git`, `gh` and `glab`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 precondition, 3 stale Foreman, 4 external (git, a gate), 5 budget or rounds. A CR argument takes its bare number (`<n>`, `CR-<n>`). Heads are full 40-character SHAs. The long gate is `gate <cr> <name>`: one name per argument, from `long_gate.commands`; it has passed at a head when the last run there passed and the head did not move. `handback <cr> ready` needs a passed gate and a `VERIFIED` verdict at the PR's head, committed, clean and pushed; `--no-gate "<the rule>"` waives the gate check only, for a project whose rules name none or name a pipeline job.

It runs no git command that changes anything (it reads the head, the remote and the status to say what is off) and no forge command beyond `forge-stack` and the reads of `ship`, `take`, `round` and `handoff`. The agents create worktrees, commit, rebase, push, open, watch and merge PRs, clean up and fast-forward the main checkout after a recorded merge, with `git`, `gh` and `glab`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 precondition (the message says which), 3 a stale Foreman (a later one claimed the batch), 4 external (git, a gate; a head that moved), 5 the budget (`take`, `round`) or the round limit (`round`). A CR argument takes its bare number (`<n>`, `CR-<n>`, `cr-<n>`). Heads are full 40-character SHAs (7 only for display; an older short record matches by prefix). The long gate is `gate <cr> <name>`: one name per argument, never a `;` or `&&` chain, from `long_gate.commands` in the code repository's root `chantier.yaml` (a surface's are ignored); it stops at the first failure and has passed at a head when the last run there passed every command and the head did not move; its log's first line names the CR, branch and full SHA, its last the result. The Verifier's `verdict <cr> VERIFIED` or `verdict <cr> "NOT VERIFIED"` is recorded at the head it verified; the last at a head decides. `handback <cr> ready` needs a passed gate and a `VERIFIED` verdict at the PR's head (or carried over a clean rebase), committed, clean and pushed; `--no-gate "<the rule>"` waives the gate check only, for a project whose rules declare none, exempt this CR, or name a pipeline job as the long gate, and the steering session checks it.

The Spec-writer and the Spec critic are subagents of the Chief of Staff or a Griller, outside any batch: each reads its own card, never `driver.md`, its brief gives the CR folder, and it takes no slot or budget (the Spec-writer writes `03-change-spec.md` there; the critic writes nothing). An agent that ends before its part is done is restarted once from the recorded state, after the parent records the cause (`note <cr> "restart: <cause>"`): `stopped from outside`, `host failure: <text>`, `refused first line`, `reply out of format: <what>`, a mode switch, or a cause the Foreman's card names.

An agent that ends before its part is done (any agent, any parent) is restarted once from the recorded state (`handoff`, `log`, the CR's notes, the worktree's commits, the folder's files), after the parent records the cause (`note <cr> "restart: <cause>"`; for a spec-writer or critic, its `work/specifying` line; for a retro critic, in the parent's own words in its turn): `stopped from outside: <text>`, `host failure: <exact text>`, `refused first line`, `reply out of format: <what>`, `switch to Foreman mode`, `switch to direct mode`, or a cause `help lost-restart` names (`context`, a proven death, a new epoch, a silent end).

- Only `coder`, `debugger` and `conflict-resolver` escalate. Drivers never do (a failed restack escalates the stack driver's `conflict-resolver`; the stack driver keeps the batch's model); nor do the judging agents (`inspector`, `verifier`, `investigator`, `spec-writer`, `spec-critic`, `retro-critic`, `demo-explorer`): a new one runs on its own model.
concepts.md

- Triggers: a `blocked rounds:` hand-back (the next rounds' Coder); two `blocked` hand-backs of one CR that show trouble in the work; a red check the Debugger could not explain; a conflict the resolver could not settle.

- Triggers, and who acts:
  - a `blocked rounds:` hand-back, any failure: once the user grants rounds, the CR's next Driver is told `escalate: rounds` and starts each new round's Coder on the escalation model (a grant with a `rounds exception:` note keeps the model); escalation never grants a round.
  - two `blocked` hand-backs of one CR that show trouble in the work (`refused`, `infra:` after its re-runs, `driver ended twice`, `stopped`, `rounds:` not under the exception, `fix:`; never `question:`, `approval:`, `merge:`, `waits:`, `budget:` or a stop from outside), when the row above did not escalate: the Foreman (direct: the Chief of Staff), from `log <cr>`, runs `take <cr> --note "escalate: blocked twice: <reasons>"`; a CR with no rounds (release, QA order, `fix:`) goes to the user's question.
  - a red check the Debugger could not explain (its `diagnosis.md` names no cause with evidence): its Driver starts a new `debugger` given that file.
  - a conflict the resolver could not settle (two product intents stay a user question): its Driver starts a new `conflict-resolver` given `conflicts.md`.
  - a Debugger fix that fails again, or a stack driver's red check needing code (`anomaly`), ends in CR hand-backs.

- Once per CR, then the user: a CR with an `escalated:` note made for that CR (not a stack-wide one written on each CR) never escalates again nor swaps back; if it fails again it stays `blocked`, is not taken again, and goes up as a question (one more round, drop it, another approach), with no further round without the answer; so does a CR with no rounds blocked twice.
